section.name: General
section.p: As a headless browser, HtmlUnit does not display images. Most of the time it doesn't even have to look inside an image. There are some exceptions where HtmlUnit has to decode the image:

ul.li: reading the real size of an image, e.g. via the width, height, naturalWidth or naturalHeight properties, or HtmlImage.getWidth() / HtmlImage.getHeight(); the size is also used for layout related methods like Element.getBoundingClientRect()
drawing an image onto a canvas with CanvasRenderingContext2D.drawImage()

section.p: For decoding, HtmlUnit uses Java's ImageIO. Out of the box, ImageIO supports JPEG, PNG, BMP, WBMP, GIF and TIFF.

section.name: When are images downloaded
section.p: To save time and bandwidth, HtmlUnit downloads an image only if

ul.li: the image element has an onload or onerror handler (and JavaScript is enabled),
the image is needed for one of the cases listed above, or
you enabled the download of all images with webClient.getOptions().setDownloadImages(true).

section.p: Downloading the image is not the same as decoding it. HtmlImage.saveAs(File), for example, works for every format.

section.name: Unsupported image formats
section.p: If ImageIO has no reader for the format of an image (e.g. SVG or WebP), HtmlUnit behaves like this:

ul.li: width and height report the size of a broken image icon (depending on the simulated browser), naturalWidth and naturalHeight are 0.
drawImage() draws nothing and logs an INFO message that points to this page.
The load event depends only on the download. It is fired even if the image can't be decoded, while real browsers fire an error event in this case.

section.p: To overcome this limitation, you can add ImageIO plugins to the classpath. They are found automatically, no HtmlUnit configuration is required. The TwelveMonkeys project provides plugins for many formats, e.g. WebP, SVG, ICO and PSD.

subsection.name: SVG
subsection.p: The TwelveMonkeys SVG plugin is a wrapper for Apache Batik. Batik is not included, you have to add it yourself:
subsection.source: <dependency> <groupId>com.twelvemonkeys.imageio</groupId> <artifactId>imageio-batik</artifactId> <version>3.15.3</version> </dependency> <dependency> <groupId>org.apache.xmlgraphics</groupId> <artifactId>batik-transcoder</artifactId> <version>1.20</version> <exclusions> <!-- HtmlUnit already depends on commons-io and commons-logging --> <exclusion> <groupId>commons-io</groupId> <artifactId>commons-io</artifactId> </exclusion> <exclusion> <groupId>commons-logging</groupId> <artifactId>commons-logging</artifactId> </exclusion> <!-- the JDK already contains these XML APIs --> <exclusion> <groupId>xml-apis</groupId> <artifactId>xml-apis</artifactId> </exclusion> </exclusions> </dependency>
subsection.p: Batik is a large library and has had several security issues in the past (see Apache XML Graphics Security). Use the latest version, and add it only if you need SVG images on a canvas or their size.

section.name: Android
section.p: ImageIO is not available on Android. There, HtmlUnit doesn't decode images at all and reports a size of 0 x 0.
